products.metadata_one_value: The NOAA Coral Reef Watch (CRW) weekly Four-Month Coral Bleaching Outlook product (version 5.0) was released publicly on March 27, 2018, after being made available on November 21, 2017. This Outlook, updated weekly, utilizes daily sea surface temperature forecasts from NOAA/NCEP's Climate Forecast System Version 2 (CFSv2), a comprehensive ocean-land-atmosphere climate model. products.copyright: Please contact the provider of this data for more information, including information about usage rights and constraints.
products.metadata_one_value: The hourly tide predictions (in meters) are produced under the Pacific Sea Level and Geodetic Monitoring (PSLGM) component of the Climate and Oceans Support Program in the Pacific (COSPPac). Tide predictions for a specific location are derived from historical sea level records, which require a minimum of 35 days of observations at that site. By analyzing the dominant harmonic components of these records, accurate tidal forecasts can be generated. These predictions are also compiled into tidal calendars and made available for countries across the Pacific region through COSPPac.

products.name: Pacific Ocean - All Observation Network

products.metadata_one_value: This dataset includes measurements from three ocean monitoring instruments: DART (Deep-ocean Assessment and Reporting of Tsunamis) buoys, wave buoys, and tide gauges. DART buoys detect tsunami activity in real time using seabed pressure sensors and surface buoys, with data transmitted via satellite telemetry to tsunami warning centers. Wave buoys record ocean wave characteristics such as height, period, and direction, supporting marine forecasting and safety. Tide gauges measure sea level changes along coastlines, providing essential information for tide prediction, sea-level monitoring, and coastal hazard assessment. All instruments use satellite telemetry to transmit data in real time.

products.name: Marine Heat Wave
products.copyright: Please contact the provider of this data for more information, including information about usage rights and constraints.
products.metadata_one_value: The daily global 5 km-resolution Marine Heat Wave (MHW) product presented here is a generalized adaptation of NOAA’s Coral Reef Watch (CRW) daily 5 km Coral Bleaching HotSpot product. Unlike the coral-specific product, this MHW dataset describes oceanic heat stress broadly, occurring at any time of year and affecting a wide range of marine life. The product is derived using the Marine Heatwave algorithm of Hobday et al. (2018) applied to the CRW daily 5 km CoralTemp satellite SST dataset. It includes both near real-time and historical data, spanning 1985 to the present.
products.metadata_two_value: Marine Heatwaves are prolonged periods of anomalously high sea surface temperature (SST). In effect, they are categorized anomalies of SST compared with a long-term, high, daily SST threshold.

products.name: Altimetry
products.copyright: Please contact the provider of this data for more information, including information about usage rights and constraints.
products.metadata_one_value: Dating from 1993, satellite altimeter data provide a global perspective of sea level, enabling the tide gauge data to be placed in context. Three satellites have been used: TOPEX/Poseidon, Jason-1 and OSTM/Jason-2. They each reference a different height datum – see Church and White (2011) for more information. Data is available as a monthly mean anomaly (in millimetres) with the latest updated spanning the period January 1993 to July 2020, which will be periodically updated. Please note that inverse barometer correction (IB), seasonal signal and Global trend are not removed while Glazial isostatic adjustment (GIA) is removed.
products.metadata_six_value: Climate Monitoring/Ocean Dynamics/Weather and Wave Forecasting
products.metadata_seven_value: Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation (CSIRO)

products.name: Reconstruction
products.copyright: Please contact the provider of this data for more information, including information about usage rights and constraints.
products.metadata_one_value: Using relationships between a historical global tide gauge network and satellite altimetry in the recent record, Church et al. (2004) have developed a technique to reconstruct the spatial data back in time prior to the satellite era. Data are available as a monthly mean anomaly (in mm), spanning the period  from January 1950 to December 2012, which will be periodically updated. Both the altimetry and  reconstruction gridded datasets have a 1° (latitude) by 1° (longitude) resolution over the region from  60°E to 210°E, and from 15°N to 65°S.

products.name: Significant Wave Height
products.copyright: Please contact the provider of this data for more information, including information about usage rights and constraints.
products.metadata_one_value: The Global Wave Hindcast is a model-based reconstruction of ocean wave conditions spanning from the late 1970s to the present. It provides a consistent, quality-controlled dataset of wave height, period, and direction, with special attention to the Australian and Pacific Island regions. The Bureau of Meteorology and CSIRO developed the hindcast model, known as the CAWCR (Centre for Australian Weather and Climate Research) Wave Hindcast, with the primary objective of providing global data at higher resolution, focused on Australia and the central and southwest Pacific region (Durrant et al., 2014). The hindcast data is provided as it is and is a subset of the original domain.
products.metadata_six_value: Model Development and Validation/Wave Climate and Coastal Engineering/Wave Energy Resource Assessment
